page: Microsoft Azure D4ads_v6 is a general-purpose virtual machine powered by an AMD EPYC 9V74 processor based on the x86_64 architecture. Running on the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor, this instance provides 4 dedicated vCPUs mapped from 2 physical cores with hyper-threading enabled. The processor operates at a clock speed of 3.7 GHz and features 32 KB L1d cache, 1.0 MB L2 cache, and 32 MB L3 cache. System memory totals 16.0 GB, yielding a balanced 4.0 GB of RAM per vCPU. Storage is supported by a 236 GB local disk with Premium Storage capabilities, while there are no bundled GPUs or complimentary public IPv4 addresses.

Benchmark data indicates strong single-core performance, with the stress-ng single-core test scoring 3079.47 and the Geekbench single-core test reaching 2101.0, both placing in the top 25%. Multi-core performance is moderate, as evidenced by a stress-ng multi-core score of 6156.76 and a Geekbench multi-core score of 4806.0. However, memory bandwidth is a notable bottleneck; read-only bandwidth for both small and large blocks falls into the bottom 25%, measuring 303.66 GB/sec and 37.93 GB/sec respectively. Similarly, multi-threaded bzip3 decompression and PassMark database operations show weaker performance profiles, placing in the lower quartile.

This server configuration is suited for workloads that benefit from high single-core CPU speeds but do not demand intensive memory throughput or massive multi-threaded scaling. Appropriate applications include static web serving, which achieved a throughput of 6.43 GB/sec, and lightweight Redis deployments, processing 5.92 million SET operations per second. The hardware profile offers a cost-efficient balance of dedicated compute and local storage for general-purpose tasks, though it is poorly suited for complex tasks like medium-scale LLM inference, where prompt processing speeds drop to 11.76 tokens/second.

It includes a 236 GB local disk with Premium Storage capabilities but lacks a GPU. Benchmarks show strong single-core capabilities, with Geekbench single-core scores in the top 25%, though multi-core performance and memory read bandwidth are weaker, placing in the bottom 25%. This resource profile makes the instance suitable for general-purpose workloads such as static web serving, text processing, and lightweight database operations, offering a balanced compute-to-memory ratio for applications that do not require high memory throughput or heavy multi-threaded scaling.
